podcast.body: Even though this song is not directly about Boogie Woogie, it incorporates the Boogie rhythm and features nods to the generic Boogie bass line. It also contains lines like, "when you hear that whistle blowing eight to the bar, then you know that Tennessee is not very far," highlighting the pervasive influence of Boogie Woogie in popular music of the early 1940s. podcast.body: This single was awarded the first recorded gold record in February 1942 by RCA. By that time, the song had sold an astonishing 1.2 million units, an incredible feat for the 1940s given the marketing and distribution challenges of the era.
